name: Alfred Russel Wallace
summary: British naturalist and co-discoverer of natural selection, known as the father of biogeography.

name: Charles Darwin
summary: British naturalist and co-discoverer of natural selection.

name: Henry Walter Bates
summary: British naturalist and explorer, colleague of Wallace in Brazil.

name: Charles Lyell
summary: British geologist and friend of Darwin who advised on the joint reading of evolutionary papers.

name: Joseph Hooker
summary: British botanist and friend of Darwin who advised on the joint reading of evolutionary papers.

name: T. H. Huxley
summary: British biologist who coined the term 'Wallace's Line'.

name: Percival Lowell
summary: American astronomer who argued for canals on Mars, debated by Wallace.

name: Robert Owen
summary: Utopian socialist whose teachings influenced Wallace.

name: P. L. Sclater
summary: Zoologist whose biogeographical region scheme Wallace adopted.

name: Royal Geographical Society
summary: Organization that granted Wallace funding for his travel to Singapore.

name: Linnean Society of London
summary: Scientific society where the joint Darwin-Wallace paper on natural selection was read.

name: Land Nationalisation Society
summary: Organization where Wallace served as president for over thirty years.

name: Usk, Monmouthshire
summary: Town in Wales where Wallace was born.

name: England
summary: Country where Wallace spent much of his life.

name: Wales
summary: Country where Wallace worked as a surveyor in his youth.

name: London
summary: City where Wallace moved as a teenager and later returned.

name: Leicester
summary: City in England where Wallace worked as a school instructor.

name: Pará (Belém)
summary: City at the mouth of the Amazon where Wallace arrived in 1848.

name: Singapore
summary: Location Wallace moved to before exploring the Malay Archipelago.

name: Malay Archipelago
summary: Region Wallace explored for eight years.

name: Sarawak
summary: Location in Borneo where Wallace wrote his 1855 paper.

name: Ternate
summary: Island in the Moluccas where Wallace drafted his 1858 essay on natural selection.

name: On the Law which Has Regulated the Introduction of New Species
summary: Wallace's 1855 paper hinting at evolutionary interpretation.

name: On the Tendency of Varieties to Depart Indefinitely from the Original Type
summary: Wallace's 1858 essay outlining natural selection.

name: The Malay Archipelago
summary: Wallace's 1869 book accounting of his travels.

name: The Geographical Distribution of Animals
summary: Wallace's 1876 two-volume standard work on biogeography.

name: Tropical Nature and Other Essays
summary: Wallace's 1878 contribution to ecological biogeography.

name: Island Life
summary: Wallace's 1880 work on insular faunas and floras.

name: Is Mars Habitable?
summary: Wallace's 1907 volume debunking Lowell's theory of Martians.
